_about: State discrepancies that are real, already happened, and cannot be honestly reconstructed. Each entry is an exception list read by tools/check_runtime_integrity.py. An entry excuses exactly the named strategy_id and nothing else, so a new occurrence of the same class of failure still fails the gate. Entries are not permission to repeat a defect.

known_missing.evidence: STRATEGY_ADMISSION_REVIEWED accepted=true in runtime/autopoiesis/journal.jsonl; no file in runtime/autopoiesis/strategies/; no STRATEGY_LIFECYCLE_UPDATED with new_lifecycle=RETIRED naming it.
known_missing.cause: UNKNOWN. runtime/ is gitignored, so there is no commit history to reconstruct when or why the file was removed. Recording a cause here would be a fabrication.
known_missing.cannot_recur_because: strategy_admission.admit() writes the spec atomically (write_text_atomic under a file lock) BEFORE returning accepted=True, and the daemon journals the event only after admit() returns. A journalled acceptance therefore implies a durable file.

not_a_finding.why: A rejected proposal correctly has no registry file. An earlier version of the integrity check flagged these as missing, which was the check being wrong, not the data.
A cycle_id on a reflection or evaluation event is a foreign key, not a duplicate cycle. An earlier version counted these as double-writes and reported 228 phantom duplicates.
